### Observed differences

- The relative order of two groups of activities flipped. In the earlier window, A26 and A27 came before A19, A20 and A25 in roughly 31–38 of 100 traces, and the reverse order never occurred; in the later window, A19, A20 and A25 come before A26 and A27 in about 30–36 of 100 traces, while the old order has essentially disappeared (at most about 1 in 200). [REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006]
- A19, A20 and A25 now occur around one-third of the way through the trace (mean positions about 0.32–0.34, down from about 0.60–0.61), while A26, A27 and A28 shifted slightly later (by about 0.02–0.04). Their participation stayed similar (about 31–39 of 100 traces in both windows), so this is a repositioning, not appearance or disappearance. [POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005, POS006]
- Routing around this segment changed. A19, A20 and A25 now lead to A26 in about 88–94 of 100 of their outgoing transitions, where before they led mainly to A28 and A32 (roughly half each). A45, which previously led to A26 in about 85 of 100 transitions, now leads to A19, A20 or A25 (about 27–29 of 100 each). A27 now leads almost only to A28 (about 98 of 100, up from 47) and A28 almost only to A32 (about 96 of 100, up from 50). [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, DIR006]
- Distances changed accordingly: A27→A28 and A28→A32 became almost always immediately consecutive (lag 1 in about 98 and 96 of 100 cases, up from about half), A27→A32 moved from lag 3 to lag 2, and A45→A26 is no longer immediate (lag 1 in about 86 of 100 before, lag 2–3 after). The old close transitions A19→A32, A25→A28 and A25→A32 nearly vanished (76, 33 and 61 supporting traces before versus 1, 1 and 3 after), though the after profiles rest on only 1–3 observations. [LAG001, LAG002, LAG003, LAG004, LAG005, LAG006, LAG007]
- A15 still occurs in every trace but repeats less often: mean occurrences per trace fell from about 1.9 to about 1.6, and the share of traces in which it recurs fell from about 47 to 38 in 100. [OCC001]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that the segment formed by A19, A20 and A25 was relocated to earlier in the process: in the later window it runs before A26 and A27, is entered from A45, and leads into A26, while A27, A28 and A32 form a tight sequential chain (A27→A28→A32). Separately, A15 is repeated less often. [REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006, POS001, POS002, POS003, DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR006, LAG004, LAG005, LAG006, LAG007, OCC001]

The order reversal is shown directly by relational evidence in all six activity pairs, always in the same direction, with the old order almost completely absent; the positional shifts and successor changes agree with it; and the number of qualifying items (26, against about 0.6 expected if nothing had changed) means chance cannot explain the evidence as a whole. [REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006, POS001, POS002, POS003, DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, DIR006, LAG004, LAG005, LAG006, LAG007]

Limitations: the after profiles of the vanished close transitions rest on only 1–3 observations; several items describe the same underlying traces (the six relational pairs cover one flip, and the routing items overlap), so they are not independent confirmations; and the evidence cannot separate a rewiring within one process from a wholesale shift in the mix of process variants — for example an early-segment variant absent from the first sample replacing a late-segment one — nor other sampling differences in variant frequencies. No observed relation links the reduced repetition of A15 to the relocation. [LAG001, LAG002, LAG003, REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006, DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR006, OCC001]
